slot.brief: Arrange given alkyl/benzyl/allyl radicals in order of stability with reasoning on hyperconjugation and resonance; pick the correct series from options.

stem: Arrange the following radicals in decreasing order of stability: diphenylmethyl, cyclopent-2-en-1-yl, tert-butyl and isopropyl.

verdicts.working: Diphenylmethyl is resonance-stabilized by two phenyl rings; cyclopent-2-en-1-yl is allylic. Among the alkyl radicals, tert-butyl is more stable than isopropyl due to greater hyperconjugation. Thus the order is (A).

working:
Diphenylmethyl and cyclopent-2-en-1-yl radicals are resonance-stabilised.
Two phenyl rings delocalise the diphenylmethyl radical more extensively than the allylic ring system.
For alkyl radicals, hyperconjugation gives tert-butyl > isopropyl.
Hence: diphenylmethyl > cyclopent-2-en-1-yl > tert-butyl > isopropyl.

Independent check: Diphenylmethyl is resonance-stabilized by two phenyl rings; cyclopent-2-en-1-yl is allylic. Among the alkyl radicals, tert-butyl is more stable than isopropyl due to greater hyperconjugation. Thus the order is (A).
solution:
Resonance stabilisation makes diphenylmethyl and the allylic cyclopent-2-en-1-yl radical more stable than alkyl radicals; delocalisation over two phenyl rings stabilises diphenylmethyl most. Among alkyl radicals, greater hyperconjugation stabilises tert-butyl over isopropyl.
$$\text{Diphenylmethyl} > \text{cyclopent-2-en-1-yl} > \text{tert-butyl} > \text{isopropyl}$$
